A.explanation: Gives $1.13 \text{kPa}$ by using $\rho \times h$ with $h = 0.10 \text{ m}$ and omitting $g$, so it is not a pressure from a weight.

B.explanation: Gives $1.70 \text{kPa}$ by using $\rho \times h$ with $h = 0.15 \text{ m}$ and omitting $g$, so the force is missing the factor $9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.

C.explanation: Gives $11.1 \text{kPa}$ from $p = \rho g h$ with the smallest height $h = 0.10 \text{ m}$, which is the minimum pressure, not the maximum.

D.explanation: Gives $16.6 \text{kPa}$ from $p = \rho g h$ with the largest height $h = 0.15 \text{ m}$, which gives the smallest base area and largest pressure.

hints: Notice the word maximum: for the same weight, pressure $p = F/A$ is largest when the contact area $A$ with the table is smallest.
For a block, $F = mg$ with $m = \rho V$, so $p = \rho V g / A = \rho g h$ where $h$ is the vertical height of the $12.0 \text{ cm}$, $15.0 \text{ cm}$ and $10.0 \text{ cm}$ sides.
Choose the $15.0 \text{ cm}$ side as the vertical height, convert it to metres, then evaluate $p = (1.13 \times 10^4) \times 9.81 \times h$ and convert pascals to kilopascals.
walkthrough: Weight is fixed, so from $p = F/A$ maximum pressure needs minimum contact area. That means resting on the $12.0 \text{ cm} \times 10.0 \text{ cm}$ face so the $15.0 \text{ cm}$ side is vertical.
Use $p = F/A$ with $F = mg$ and $m = \rho V$. With $V = A \times h$, the area cancels to give $p = \rho g h$.
Convert the maximum height to metres: $h = 15.0 \text{ cm} = 0.150 \text{ m}$. Use $\rho = 1.13 \times 10^4 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ and $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.
Convert to kilopascals: $1.66 \times 10^4 \text{ Pa} \approx 16.6 \text{ kPa}$. This is option D.
